note: Sample Paper has only 20 MC. No official marking scheme: all Section B answers are Quest's own, labelled 'Suggested answer:'. Q1(d) carries 4 marks in total; the (i)/(ii) split is not printed, 1/3 assumed.

mc.q: To create a web page with Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese characters, which of the following methods is/are possible?
st: Use Unicode on the web page.
Use both BIG5 and GB on the web page.
Use BIG5 to represent traditional Chinese characters and image files to display simplified Chinese characters.
mc.exp: One page can only declare one encoding, so mixing BIG5 and GB fails. Unicode covers both; images also work.

mc.q: The hardware address of a network device consists of 48 bits. Which of the following is a valid address in hexadecimal numbers?
mc.exp: 48 bits = 12 hex digits. C has 'G', not a hex digit.

mc.q:
[Slide shown: PROGRAMME — Talk 1 The Examination System in Hong Kong, Dr. Chan Tai Man（陳大文博士）, 15 minutes; Talk 2 The Examination System in China, Dr. Kwai Wing（季榮博士）, 20 minutes; Talk 3 The Examination System in Singapore, Dr. Sen Kit（孫潔博士）, 25 minutes; Talk 4 The Examination System in South Korea, Dr. Lee Kim King（李金京博士）, 30 minutes; Total : 90 minutes]
When using a presentation software package, which of the following may be used to prepare the above slide efficiently?
mc.exp: The slide repeats the same pattern ("The Examination System in …", "Dr. …"), so copy-and-paste then find-and-replace saves typing. The table borders are part of the layout, not what makes it efficient.

mc.q: Which of the following is not a specification of a CPU?
mc.exp: Rotational latency describes a hard disk.

mc.q: Which of the following is not open source software?
mc.exp: Internet Explorer is proprietary freeware, not open source.

mc.q: When compared with normal PCs, which of the following statements about Personal Digital Assistants (PDA) is correct?
o: Only small files can be stored.
The operating system requires less system memory to operate.
The operating system should be re-installed when the system crashes.
Data must be stored in an external flash memory card.
mc.exp: Mobile OSs are designed to run in less memory.

mc.q: Which of the following actions should not be carried out when constructing a web page?
o: Insert multimedia elements but not photos.
mc.exp: HTML is interpreted by the browser, never compiled.

mc.q:
The following algorithm shows how a vending machine works:
Step 1: Wait to receive a coin.
Step 2: If the coin is not $1, $2, $5 or $10, eject it.
Step 3: If $6 or more is deposited, do steps 4 and 5.
Step 4:     Release a can of lemon tea.
Step 5:     Reduce the deposit by $6.
Step 6: Eject the deposit.
Step 7: Do step 1.
Which of the following statements about the algorithm is true?
o: A can of lemon tea will cost less than $6.
The vending machine will release lemon tea.
A can of lemon tea will cost more than $6.
The vending machine will release lemon tea only if a $10 coin is received.
mc.exp: Step 6 ejects the deposit after EVERY coin, so the deposit never builds up. Only a single $10 coin reaches $6.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about copyright is correct?
o: It is effective only if the author has a statement about copyright on his/her work.
It applies to computer software only.
The author must register his/her work to obtain copyright.
It applies automatically to the owner of the original work.
mc.exp: In Hong Kong copyright arises automatically; no registration or notice needed.

mc.q: What is the minimum number of bits needed to represent a set of 94 characters of 'Hangul' in the Korean language?
Jimmy wants to include some multimedia elements in a presentation file. Instead of copying the multimedia elements into the file, he uses hyperlinks. Which of the following descriptions is correct?
o: The presentation can include more multimedia elements.
The presentation can be more interactive.
The presentation can play video files immediately.
mc.exp: Linked media stays outside the file.

mc.q:
A 3×3 table is created in spreadsheet software and the preview of the printout is shown below:
[print preview figure]
Which of the following actions is the most appropriate way to improve the presentation of the table?
o: Change the horizontal alignment of the cells in the table.
mc.exp: Per the official key (B): the table does not fit the page width in the preview, so switching to landscape lets it print on one page.

mc.q: Which of the following I/O devices are commonly used by a cashier in a restaurant?
mc.exp: Card reader for payment, thermal printer for receipts.

mc.q: Which of the following is not an online public service provided by ESDlife（生活易）?
o: Booking an appointment to give a marriage notice
mc.exp: Per the official key (B): booking a (private) dentist appointment was not one of ESDlife's government e-services; the others were.

mc.q: Mr. Chan wants to register a domain name using his name, 'Chan Tai Man'. Which of the following domain names is not valid?
mc.exp: .com.org is not a real second/top-level combination. Domain names are case-insensitive.

mc.q:
Lily tells her friends, Ka Kee (KaKee@hkeaa.edu.hk), Po Yan (PoYan@hkeaa.edu.hk) and Mo Yi (MoYi@hkeaa.edu.hk), the date of her birthday party through an email:
To: KaKee@hkeaa.edu.hk
CC: PoYan@hkeaa.edu.hk
BCC: MoYi@hkeaa.edu.hk
SUBJECT: My birthday party on 25/4
Which of the following statements cannot be derived from this email?
o: Ka Kee knows that the birthday party is held on 25/4.
Ka Kee knows that Po Yan receives the email.
Po Yan knows that Mo Yi receives the email.
Mo Yi knows that Ka Kee and Po Yan receive the email.
mc.exp: BCC recipients are hidden from everyone else.

mc.q:
[Browser screenshot: some Chinese characters marked 'correct display', others 'incorrect display']
The above screen shot of a browser, shows that some Chinese characters are correctly displayed while some are not. Which of the following is the possible reason?
o: The server uses two different coding schemes to store the Chinese characters of the web page.
The server uses two different protocols to send the web page to the browser.
The browser uses two different coding schemes to decode the Chinese characters on the web page.
The correct display is an image.
mc.exp: A browser decodes a page with one encoding, so text in another encoding is garbled; text that still looks right must be an image.

mc.q: Which of the following characteristics of high level language reflects the concept of program modules?
Amy owns a domain name, 'amycomp.com'. Which of the following URLs is not owned by Amy?
The specification of a CPU, 3.0 GHz, indicates __________________.
mc.exp: Clock rate is a measure of processing speed.

lq.stem:
(Modified from 2007 ASCA1/ALCS1 Q.8)
Mary uses her desktop computer at home to analyse a survey.

parts.q: Mary suspects that her computer is infected by spyware. Give two unusual events that may alert her to this possible infection.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Any two: pop-up advertisements keep appearing even when no browser is open; the browser home page / search engine is changed without her permission; new toolbars or unknown programs appear; the computer / Internet connection becomes unusually slow; network activity even when idle.

parts.q: After completing the analysis, Mary prepares her findings in PDF file format and posts the file onto her web site for the public to download. Give two reasons to support her use of this file format.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Any two: the layout and formatting look the same on any computer / platform; the free PDF reader is widely available, so users need not own the original software; the file can be protected against editing/copying (read-only, password); PDF files are compressed, so they are smaller to download.

parts.q: Mary also shows her findings using presentation software. Suggest three precautions which should be taken when including text in a presentation.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Any three: use a large enough font size so the audience at the back can read it; keep text short (key points / bullet points, not long paragraphs); use a clear, consistent font (avoid too many font types); keep good contrast between text colour and background; check spelling and grammar.

parts.q:
After the presentation, Mary decides to collect more views from respondents and sends them each a questionnaire by postal mail, for which a name label is required. The name and sex of each respondent are stored in a worksheet and part of the worksheet is shown below.
ABCD
1SEXFIRSTNAMELASTNAME
2FMayChan
3MJohnWong
4FAmyHo

F and M in column A represent female and male respectively. Each name label should include the title of each respondent before his or her name, for example, Ms May Chan, Mr John Wong and Ms Amy Ho.
Mary used the following steps in a word processor to create the labels.
(1) Use ‘mail merge’ with columns, SEX, FIRSTNAME and LASTNAME, as fields.
(2) Produce a merged document containing all the name labels.
(3) Use ‘find and replace’ in order to add the titles of respondents.
Instead of “Ms May Chan”, the label shows “Mrs Mray Chan”. Explain why.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: She replaced every ‘M’ with ‘Mr’ (and every ‘F’ with ‘Ms’) without choosing ‘find whole word only’ / ‘match case’. So the F was first changed to ‘Ms’, then the ‘M’ in ‘Ms’ and the ‘M’ in ‘May’ were also replaced with ‘Mr’, giving ‘Mrs Mray’. [(d) carries 4 marks in total; the split between (i) and (ii) is not printed.]

parts.q: By making use of formula(e) in the spreadsheet, describe how to add the titles of respondents, ‘Mr’ and ‘Ms’, in column D of the worksheet.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Enter in D2: =IF(A2="M","Mr","Ms") (or =IF(A2="F","Ms","Mr")); copy/fill D2 down to the last row. Then use column D (title) as a mail merge field before FIRSTNAME and LASTNAME, so no find-and-replace is needed. (Or build the whole label in one cell: =IF(A2="M","Mr ","Ms ")&B2&" "&C2.)

parts.q:
Mary uses spreadsheet software to store the responses from 40 copies of the questionnaire. Each copy consists of 6 questions. The responses to the questions are coded as values: 1, 2, 3 or 4. The following worksheet is used to record the responses.
ABCDEFGHI
1Questionnaire \ QuestionQ1Q2Q3Q4Q5Q6
2Copy 1112214
3Copy 2124433
4Copy 313123
5Copy 442324
6Copy 5244123
::::::::
41Copy 40244233
42
43Mean response score1.83.03.12.32.82.7Total number of copies
44
45Total number of ‘1’ and ‘2’25105231718
46Total number of ‘3’ and ‘4’143034142312
47
48Overall responseBADGOODGOODBADGOODBAD

When some responses are missing, the corresponding cells in the worksheet are left blank (e.g. D4). To calculate the total number of copies without any missing responses, firstly a formula is entered into I2 and then copied into I3 to I41. Secondly, another formula, ‘=SUM(I2:I41)’, is entered into I43.
Write the formula in I2.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: =IF(COUNT(B2:G2)=6,1,0) (or =IF(COUNTBLANK(B2:G2)=0,1,0)) — gives 1 for a complete copy, 0 otherwise, so SUM(I2:I41) counts the complete copies.

parts.q:
The mean response score of a question is defined as:
Mean response score = Sum of all values of the responses on that question / No. of responses on that question
where the mean response score is correct to 1 decimal place.
A formula is entered into B43, and then copied into C43 to G43, to find the mean response score for each question. Write the formula in B43.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: =ROUND(AVERAGE(B2:B41),1) (or =ROUND(SUM(B2:B41)/COUNT(B2:B41),1)). AVERAGE/COUNT ignore blank cells, so missing responses are not counted.

parts.q:
A formula, ‘=FREQUENCY(B2:B41, 2)’, is used so that the total number of responses ‘1’ and ‘2’ and the total number of responses ‘3’ and ‘4’ for each question can be found in row 45 and row 46 respectively.
How can the FREQUENCY function be entered correctly and efficiently? Describe the steps required.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: FREQUENCY is an array formula. Select the two cells B45:B46; type =FREQUENCY(B2:B41,2); press Ctrl+Shift+Enter to enter it as an array formula (B45 = count ≤2, B46 = count >2). Then copy B45:B46 across to C45:G46 (relative references adjust for each question).

parts.q:
The overall response of a question is regarded as ‘GOOD’ if it fulfills the following two conditions:
① the mean response score > 2.5
② the total number of responses ‘3’ and ‘4’ > the total number of responses ‘1’ and ‘2’
Otherwise the overall response of the question is regarded as ‘BAD’. A formula is entered into B48, and then copied into C48 to G48 to find the overall responses of the questions.
Write the formula in B48.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: =IF(AND(B43>2.5,B46>B45),"GOOD","BAD")

lq.stem:
(Modified from 2006 CECIT 1B Q.3)
David installs a desktop computer, X, and a notebook computer, Y, forming a LAN and connecting to the Internet through a 10M broadband connection in his bedroom. The configurations of the computers are as follows:
XY
CPUP4 3 GHzM 1.73 GHz
Cache2 MB2 MB
RAM512 MB256 MB
Network10/100 LAN card10/100 LAN card and 54M wireless LAN card

parts.q:
David wants to connect an external DVD writer to X.
The DVD writer is not designed to connect to a parallel port. Why not?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: A parallel port is too slow for the high data transfer rate a DVD writer needs (and is an old, bulky interface that is not hot-pluggable).

parts.q: Give the port that the DVD writer should be connected to: ______
parts.ms: Suggested answer: USB (2.0) port (also accept FireWire / IEEE 1394 / eSATA).

parts.q:
Y can be connected to the Internet through a network cable or wireless communication. Compare the performance using these two methods in the following activities in terms of data transmission speed.
File sharing between X and Y
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Cable is faster: X and Y both have 10/100 LAN cards, so wired file sharing can reach 100 Mbps, while wireless is at most 54 Mbps (X has no wireless card, so the data must also pass through the router/access point).

parts.q: Browsing the Internet
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Almost no difference: the bottleneck is the 10M broadband connection, which is slower than both the 54M wireless link and the 100M wired link.

parts.q: Cache is “high-speed” memory. In X, the size of the cache is much smaller than that of RAM. In order to enhance X’s performance, should X install 512 MB cache? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: No. Cache memory (SRAM) is very expensive, and cache size is fixed by the CPU design, so it cannot simply be added. A small cache already holds the most frequently used data/instructions; making it huge gives little extra speed for the cost.

parts.q: In order to preserve the connectivity of X and Y in the LAN, should both be installed the same version of the operating system? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: No. Computers communicate using common network protocols (e.g. TCP/IP), not a common OS, so different operating systems / versions can still share files and connect in the same LAN.

lq.stem:
(Modified from 2006 ASCA1 Q.5, 2006 ALCS2 Q.9, 2004 ALCS2 Q.8)
David creates a web page with frames and animation.
[Screenshot: left frame with links Introduction, Vision, Mission, Contact Us; right frame titled ‘Vision’ with text ‘Assessment for Learning’, a box with a broken-image icon ✕, the HKEAA logo, footer ‘HKEAA All rights reserved’, and a vertical scroll bar]

parts.q: David can successfully browse the animation in the web page on one computer but cannot browse it on another one. The web page is only displayed as shown above. Give a possible reason for this.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: The other computer’s browser lacks the required plug-in (e.g. Flash player) for the animation / does not support that file format, or the animation file’s path is a local path on David’s own computer (absolute path) so it cannot be found.

parts.q: Give one unsatisfactory aspect of the design of the above web page presentation, other than the animation.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Any one: the right frame is too small, so the user must scroll to see the content; the footer is cut off; there is no indication of which link (page) is currently selected / inconsistent layout.

parts.q:
David wants to share a file with other people. The file can be downloaded by clicking a hyperlink on the web page or by Peer-to-Peer (P2P) freeware.
Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using a hyperlink to download the file.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Advantage: easy to use; no special software is needed (only a browser), and the source is known/trusted.
Disadvantage: all downloads come from one server, so it is slow / the server may be overloaded when many people download at the same time (and uses David’s bandwidth / hosting space).

parts.q: List two social impacts of the inappropriate use of this P2P freeware.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Any two: spread of pirated software, music and films (copyright infringement, loss to creators); spread of computer viruses/malware; leakage of private data (shared folders); spread of indecent or illegal materials; heavy use of network bandwidth.

parts.q:
David studies in ACC College. In the college, an SMTP server is used to transfer e-mail with other SMTP servers over the Internet. The SMTP server stores the e-mail in a POP3 server, which allows client computers to retrieve the e-mail. Outgoing e-mail is sent directly through the SMTP server.
David gets the following information from ACC College.
POP3 E-mail Account Settings on Mail Client Software:
SMTP Server Name / IP Address: smtp.acc.edu.hk / 210.0.168.23
POP3 Server Name / IP Address: pop3.acc.edu.hk / 210.0.168.112
User Name: davidchan
Password: beasmartboy
Based on the information provided, fill in the following dialog box from the mail client software so that Peter can send and retrieve e-mail at home with the mail client software.
Server Information — Incoming mail server: ______ Outgoing mail server: ______
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Incoming mail server: pop3.acc.edu.hk (or 210.0.168.112)
Outgoing mail server: smtp.acc.edu.hk (or 210.0.168.23)

parts.q:
Normally, users configure the mail client software with the server names instead of the IP addresses.
Give an advantage of using the server name over the IP address.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: A name is easier to remember and type; and if the server’s IP address changes, the name still works (DNS is updated), so users need not change their settings.

parts.q: Give an advantage of using the IP address over the server name.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: It still works when the DNS server is down, and it is slightly faster because no DNS lookup is needed.

parts.q: Suppose the SMTP server is stopped but the POP3 server is still running. What functions with respect to sending and receiving e-mail can still be used? What functions cannot be used?
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Can still be used: retrieving / reading e-mail already stored in the POP3 server.
Cannot be used: sending any e-mail, and receiving new e-mail from outside (since incoming mail is transferred by the SMTP server into the POP3 server).

lq.stem:
(Modified from 2006 CECIT 1B Q.4)
Mr. Lam designs a simple greenhouse cooling and heating system. The ideal greenhouse temperature is between 20 °C and 32 °C. Initially, the cooler and heater are off. The system will operate as follows:
Temperature (X)Cooler (C)Heater (H)
X < 20OFFON
X > 32ONOFF

The flowchart below describes the operations of the system and Module E is a part for energy conservative.
[Flowchart: START → decision ‘____ and C is OFF’ — YES: Turn C ON; NO: continue → decision ‘____ and H is OFF’ — YES: Turn H ON; NO: continue → Module E → loop back to the first decision]

parts.q: Fill the appropriate conditions of X in the two decision boxes of the flowchart.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: First box: X > 32 (and C is OFF) → turn C ON.
Second box: X < 20 (and H is OFF) → turn H ON.

parts.q: In order to save more energy, Mr. Lam decides that the cooler will be turned off when X ≤ 28, and the heater will be turned off when 24 ≤ X. Draft a flowchart for Module E to implement his idea in the space provided. The design of Module E should be precise and without redundancy.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: Module E (written as flowchart steps):
Decision: X <= 28 and C is ON ?
   YES → Turn C OFF
   NO  → (continue)
Decision: X >= 24 and H is ON ?
   YES → Turn H OFF
   NO  → (continue)
(exit Module E)
Each decision needs both the temperature condition and the device-state check, with YES leading to the turn-OFF box and both paths joining before the next decision.

lq.stem:
(Modified from 2004 ALCS2 Q.2, 2006 ASCA1 Q.4, 2007 ASCA1 Q.7)
Peter is an IT manager in a company. He gives some suggestions for the ergonomics of a new computer room below:
(1) Use adjustable chairs
(2) Install blinds on the windows to shade the monitors nearby
(3) Create shortcut keys for the software installed in computers

parts.q: For each of the above suggestions, explain briefly how the working conditions can be ergonomically improved and state the health hazards that can be reduced.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer: (1) Users can adjust seat height/backrest to keep a good posture with feet flat and eyes level with the top of the screen → reduces back and neck pain.
(2) Blinds cut sunlight glare/reflection on the screens → reduces eye strain (and headaches).
(3) Shortcut keys reduce repeated mouse movements and clicks → reduces repetitive strain injury (RSI) of the wrist/fingers.

parts.q:
Peter is responsible for maintaining the e-mail system in the company.
To log in to the e-mail system, users are required to enter a user number and a login password.
[LOGIN form: User number: [ ] Password: [ ] Submit]
Many users enter wrong user numbers. Suggest two methods of improving the design of the system for Peter to help users enter the user numbers correctly.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Any two: add a check digit to the user number and validate it; validate the input (e.g. length / numeric-only range check) and show a clear error message; let the browser remember / provide a drop-down of the last user number; display the user’s name after the number is entered for confirmation; use a login card/smart card reader instead of typing.

parts.q: The requirement for the system’s login password changes from 6 numeric digits to 8 alphanumeric characters. Give two reasons why this change results in better security.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Longer password (8 vs 6 characters) and a larger character set (letters + digits, 36–62 symbols instead of 10) give far more possible combinations (e.g. 36^8 ≈ 2.8×10^12 vs 10^6), so brute-force attacks take much longer; alphanumeric passwords are also harder to guess than numbers such as birthdays or phone numbers.

parts.q:
Peter and his colleague, Mary, send e-mail using public and private key encryption. Peter can send e-mail to Mary using the following two methods:
① Peter encrypts an e-mail with Mary’s public key and Mary decrypts it with her own private key.
② Peter encrypts an e-mail with his own private key and Mary decrypts it with Peter’s public key.
Give an advantage of using method ①.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Confidentiality: only Mary, who holds her private key, can decrypt and read the e-mail.

parts.q: In fact, anyone can have Peter’s public key and hence can read the e-mail sent out by Peter through method ②. Why might Peter still want to use method ② ?
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Authentication / non-repudiation (digital signature): since only Peter has his private key, a message that decrypts with Peter’s public key must have come from Peter and has not been altered.

parts.q: Suggest and describe a method of using public and private key encryption which would be better than methods ① and ② for allowing Mary to read e-mail sent by Peter.
parts.ms: Suggested answer: Combine both: Peter first encrypts (signs) the e-mail with his own private key, then encrypts the result with Mary’s public key. Mary decrypts with her private key (only she can read it — confidentiality) and then with Peter’s public key (proves it came from Peter — authentication).
